I will still do wheat-maize on the same 5 mu. I have only 5 mu, so I count every bag, but I also know if fertilizer is short and yield drops, that hurts more than spending a bit extra. I do not start from zero each year. I start from what worked before and adjust a little. In my place in Quzhou, people around me doing irrigated wheat-maize usually keep wheat fertilizer a bit heavier, then maize follows after wheat harvest without wasting time. I have middle school education, so I look at the field more systematically now: wheat needs stronger base fertilizer and steady water, maize needs fast growth after sowing and enough nitrogen at jointing and bell stage. Since I have well irrigation, I will not save too hard on water for wheat. Wheat is my safer crop, so I will feed it enough to hold ears and grains. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because that is what gives stable yield around here if water keeps up. I will keep phosphorus and potassium in, not only urea, because if I push nitrogen alone the crop grows soft and I still do not get the grain I want. On pesticides, I will not spray blindly, but I will plan for two times on each crop at minimum, and maize may need one more if worms or leaf disease show up badly. On tillage, wheat season gives me enough time to rotary till after maize, but maize season is tight after wheat harvest, so I will save time with no-tillage or very light direct sowing style. That fits my labor too, because some family members work off-farm and I cannot wait around in the summer rush.
